lyrics:
Candidates
Benefactors
Friends of lawful enterprise
Kindly take your purchased places
Under rented marble skies

One point nine eight four million
Should complete what I began
Buy the books, obtain the letters
Come back as the proper man

Books have margins
Tests have keys
Deans enjoy correcting me
Every hallway has a guard
Every honest chair is hard
Years of study
Rules of form
Waiting while the ink gets warm
Why should strangers judge my claim
Why should effort define my name

Why take the test
When I can print it
Why join the school
When I can invent it
Why wait outside
And beg admission
I brought the funds
I grant permission

I grant myself the name
I sign beneath the seal
If paper bears the title
Then paper makes it real
No dean can close the gate
When I can buy the frame
I found the school
I make the rules
I grant myself the name

Rented lobby, borrowed gowns
Faculty from three small towns
Portraits painted overnight
Columns made of plaster white
Students came through magazine ads
Credit plans and proud new dads
Every course exempt from proof
Every classroom leased its roof
Dean of Strategic Denial
Chair of Blame and Countertrial
Department of Advanced Excuse
School of Other People’s Use

Why seek approval
From the able
Buy the building
Name the table
Why climb the ladder
Rung by rung
Purchase both ends
While you’re young

I grant myself the name
I sign beneath the seal
If paper bears the title
Then paper makes it real
No dean can close the gate
When I can buy the frame
I found the school
I make the rules
I grant myself the name

By authority vested in me
By property, stationery
And every privilege attached
To money properly dispatched—
Slump University hereby grants
The candidate before us
A Doctorate of Malfeasment
With full plausible deniability

I accept

Do you swear to defend the standards
You established this afternoon

Against all evidence

Against all evidence

Twelve crates arrived
No books came out
A man hung signs
And turned about
I swept the stage
I stacked each chair
No student crossed
The doorway there

Authority wears velvet sleeves
Authority has embossed leaves
Authority stands where cameras aim
Authority repeats the name
A title need not pass a test
It only needs a well-dressed guest
A photograph, a seal, a fee
And someone paid to disagree

I granted myself the name
I signed beneath the seal
The cameras caught the title
So tell me it’s not real
No dean can close the gate
No fact can spoil the frame
I own the school
I make the rules
Now say my proper name

Doctor
Doctor
Doctor Slump

Again

persona:
Michael Anthony Rose is a songwriter of rare insight and startling honesty. On his debut for Maricopa Records, he uses direct, unadorned language to explore the most profound human experiences: the gulf between who we were and who we are, the search for truth in a world of convenient fictions, and the quiet defiance of living an authentic life. His songs are less stories than they are confessions, built from the concrete details of a lived experience, where a reflection in a phone screen or the memory of a dream can trigger a lifetime of contemplation. Rose doesn't just sing about life; he holds a mirror up to it, capturing the small, resonant moments of realization that define us.

The central preoccupations of Rose's work are time and memory. His lyrics trace the lines from lost childhood potential to the stark realities of aging, questioning what we build to outlast ourselves and what we must learn to let go. He writes with a philosopher's curiosity and a diarist's intimacy, exploring the comfort of a shared lie in one song and the freedom of embracing dissonance in the next. This is music that navigates regret, loss, and mortality with a steady, empathetic gaze, always returning to the challenge of being present for the life one actually has, not the one that was planned.

Throughout his work, Rose reveals a vast emotional landscape. His voice moves from the raw vulnerability of admitting fear and bitterness to the quiet strength of asserting one’s own space and worth. He sings of intimate connection with a sensory richness and of profound disconnection with a heartbreaking clarity. His perspective is that of a seasoned witness, one who sees the innocence in younger generations without envy and accepts the limitations of his own body without surrender. He finds resilience not by ignoring the damage, but by standing within it and refusing to be diminished.

In the songs of Michael Anthony Rose, listeners will not find easy answers or false comfort. Instead, they will find a voice that speaks with clarity and courage to the complexities of a full-size life. It is an invitation to stop arguing with the truth, to witness the ordinary light of the day, and to find that being here, honestly and without shame, is more than enough.

impression.text: This track is a bombastic, highly theatrical pop-rock musical number characterized by dramatic brass arrangements, aggressive guitar riffs, and a grand, operatic vocal performance. The energy is consistently high and villainous, shifting between intense, driven rock grooves and larger-than-life, symphonic choruses that evoke a modern stage production. The production is dense and cinematic, carefully balancing punchy, modern drums and bass with a sprawling wall of brass, strings, and layered group backing vocals to maintain clarity. A particularly striking transition occurs toward the end, where the instrumentation drops out for a dark, intimate spoken-word sequence before exploding into a final, triumphant, and operatic climax.

review.review_text: This is Rose stepping fully out of the confessional and into costume, and the disguise fits better than you'd expect. A commencement organ and a snare flourish set the ceremony, then the whole thing charges ahead at a manic 152 in G minor, upright piano hammering under a self-satisfied baritone who plays both the man conferring the degree and the man receiving it. The satire is razored and specific: 'Dean of Strategic Denial, Chair of Blame and Countertrial' lands like Randy Newman writing for a Sondheim villain, and the chorus hook, 'If paper bears the title / then paper makes it real,' is the kind of line that indicts a whole culture in eleven words. The masterstroke is the ceremonial breakdown near the four-minute mark: everything drops away for a dry contralto reciting 'Twelve crates arrived / no books came out,' the one honest witness in the building, before the arrangement swells back into that oversized final chorus and the camera-shutter outro. At five-plus minutes the joke does stretch, and a second full run through the chorus tests its own welcome; this rewards the listener who sits with the whole arc rather than the one dipping in for a hook. But as a piece of character writing set to music, it holds the room. A highlight, and proof Rose can wear a mask and still tell the truth.
